html:
Kalaako and Malpa are two small Aboriginal Australian groups of the Goldfields of Western Australia, around the salt lakes near present-day Norseman. The map shows them together from 1600 to 1815. They are known mostly from the tribal map of the anthropologist Norman Tindale, and little else is written about them.

Their country lay between the Noongar peoples of the south coast, such as the Wudjari, and desert peoples to the north such as the Wangkatha. Like their neighbours they lived by hunting and gathering in dry woodland and around seasonal waterholes. The gold rushes of the 1890s at Coolgardie and Kalgoorlie, and the gold town of Norseman founded in the mid 1890s, brought miners onto this land.
